overview: The African American Civil Rights Network is a National Park Service program that links and recognizes places, programs, and facilities tied to the history of the civil rights movement. Under current law, the program's authorization lasts seven years from when Congress created it. This one-sentence bill would restart that clock, extending the program for seven years from the date this bill becomes law. As of October 29, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar for a vote.
for: Supporters say the network helps preserve and connect civil rights history sites for the public, and that a simple extension keeps an existing program running without changing how it works.
against: Critics say renewing programs without a fresh look at their results misses a chance to review whether the network is working well or should be changed.
